Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and rollout evidence, then inspect both prescribed wake views before touching the policy. I’ll also consult the fish-control-primitives skill now, as required for this transfer cycle, and record any mechanism that actually informs the edit.

The workspace requires a visual diagnosis before the edit and a final contract check without running CFD. I’m applying the “read-wake-visual-signals-first” skill for that inspection, alongside the explicitly requested bookshelf consultation.

The inherited evidence has already moved well beyond the naive seed: every sampled rollout captures, so the useful comparison is among small allocation changes around the same coherent carrier. I’m using the best sampled score (`d1fa…`) against the weakest (`e02a…`) and will check whether their trajectories are genuinely different or merely comment/schema variants before proposing anything.

The two-view check is decisive: the assigned parent’s top-down sheet shows self-propelled S-route motion with an attached alternating street through capture, and its oblique row confirms discrete 3D wake structures. The weaker sample follows nearly the same top-down route but has a blank oblique row, so it cannot support an independent 3D-wake claim. Numerically, the parent’s new half-cycle preview improves both capture time and mean distance over the no-preview baseline, while alternate response gates trade earlier crossing for a worse overall score.

The candidate will test one bounded mechanism: proximity-adaptive preview for the posterior recovery allocator. It does not add propulsion, steering amplitude, or a route; it only moves the existing fixed recovery budget between whole-carrier and velocity-quadrature targets using normalized body-frame target-line motion. This follows the bookshelf’s closed-loop CPG/phase-lag invariant, while leaving all published gains, species kinematics, and routes behind. I’m recording that hypothesis and its failure boundary before editing, as required.

The reusable guidance now incorporates the assigned parent and all sampled controls: posterior half-cycle preview is a narrow positive allocation result; anterior gate broadening and response-based release are bounded negative/tradeoff results. The policy itself changes only the recovery allocator’s prediction horizon inside the existing proximity envelope. Next I’m running the prescribed contract validator and will repair any schema or guidance failures without launching CFD.

The prescribed checker profile could not start because its configured `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable in this runtime. I did invoke it; to complete the contract, I’m now running the profile’s exact three non-CFD commands directly and will fix any failures.

The first check exposed a workspace-rendering defect rather than a candidate defect: `README.md` marks the same guidance parent twice, so the checker finds two copied-parent entries. I’m inspecting the checker’s matching rule and will repair this without changing the assigned-parent identity or solver scope.

All three prescribed non-CFD checks pass: the guidance/notes semantic check, the Julia policy contract with finite two-joint output, and the solver boundary check. I also removed the duplicated assigned-parent marker in the rendered `README.md` that had caused the checker’s initial false failure; the parent identity itself is unchanged. I’m doing one final read-only diff review now.

Produced exactly one candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl).

It adds bounded proximity-adaptive preview to the existing posterior recovery allocation without increasing authority.

Updated:

- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md)

All prescribed non-CFD checks pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract, and solver boundary. The checker agent’s configured model was unavailable, so its exact commands were run directly. No CFD was run.
